subject: Business Models
title: The Survivorship Bias Problem
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Survivorship Bias Problem.

hook.text: We study Amazon, Apple, and Google obsessively. We ignore 10,000 companies that tried the same things and failed.

buildup.text: Survivorship bias: we learn from winners and assume their strategies cause success. We don't study the dead.

discovery.text: Many failed companies did exactly what successful ones did: pivoted fast, raised capital, hired great teams.

twist.text: For every Facebook, there were 100 social networks. For every Uber, 50 ride-sharing apps. Success includes luck.

climax.text: Studying failures teaches more than studying successes. The dead reveal which strategies actually don't work.

punchline.text: For every success, 100 failures tried the same. Study the dead, not the living.

quiz.question: What is survivorship bias in business?
options: Focusing only on surviving companies and ignoring failures that used similar strategies
Companies that survive are always better

details.summary: Business literature focuses on successful companies while ignoring the thousands that failed using identical strategies. Survivorship bias creates false lessons: the strategies that worked for Amazon may have doomed hundreds of forgotten companies that tried the same approach without Amazon's.
details.whyItMatters: Survivorship bias distorts strategic thinking. Studying only winners creates a misleading map. Understanding the failures that used the same strategies as successes provides the context needed to evaluate which strategies actually work and under.
takeaways: Business strategy studies ignore the graveyard of companies using identical tactics
Successful strategies may simply reflect survivor luck, not replicable methods
Studying failures alongside successes provides more accurate strategic insight

faq.question: How does survivorship bias affect business strategy advice?
faq.answer: Books study Amazon's customer obsession or Apple's design focus and prescribe those strategies universally. But thousands of customer-obsessed and design-focused companies failed. Without studying the failures, we cannot determine whether those strategies caused success or merely correlated with it.

faq.question: How can entrepreneurs counter survivorship bias in their planning?
faq.answer: Study companies that failed using similar strategies to understand what went wrong. Look for base rates of success in your industry rather than cherry-picked examples. Focus on conditions and context that enabled success rather than generic strategies..
